question_text: A high‐strength steel has a yield strength of 1 460 MPa and a fracture toughness K_IC of 98 MPa·√m.  Assuming a through‐thickness center crack (Y = 1), determine the half‐crack length a that will cause catastrophic failure when the applied tensile stress reaches ½ Y.S.The unit of the answer is mm.
response:
The catastrophic failure condition is when the stress intensity factor reaches the fracture toughness:

$$K_{IC} = Y\,\sigma\sqrt{\pi a}$$

With $\sigma = \tfrac{1}{2}\text{Y.S.} = 730\text{ MPa}$, $Y=1$, and $K_{IC}=98\text{ MPa·√m}$:

$$a = \frac{1}{\pi}\left(\frac{K_{IC}}{Y\sigma}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{\pi}\left(\frac{98}{730}\right)^2 \approx 5.74\times10^{-3}\text{ m} = 5.74\text{ mm}$$

$$\boxed{5.74}$$
